items.title: Founding of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty & Golconda
items.body:
## From Bahmani governor to sultan

- The **Qutb Shahi dynasty** was founded in **1518** by **Quli Qutb Mulk** (Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk), the **Bahmani governor (tarafdar) of Telangana**, when the Bahmani Sultanate broke up.
- He was of **Turkoman origin**, born in **Persia**, and had earned the title **Qutb-ul-Mulk** as a Bahmani military chief.
- Golconda was one of the **five Deccan sultanates** (with Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Bidar and Berar); the dynasty ruled **1518-1687**.

## Golconda fort & diamonds

- **Golconda**, a massive **granite hill fort**, was the first capital — famed for its **water system, granaries and acoustics** (a clap at the entrance could be heard at the top).
- Golconda was the world's great **diamond emporium**; the **Kollur mine** in the Krishna valley yielded legendary stones including the **Koh-i-Noor** and the **Hope Diamond**.
- 'Golconda diamond' still denotes a stone of exceptional purity.
keyPoints: Qutb Shahi dynasty founded 1518 by Quli Qutb Mulk (Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk), the Bahmani governor of Telangana.
Founder was of Turkoman origin, born in Persia; title Qutb-ul-Mulk earned under the Bahmanis.
Golconda was one of the five Deccan sultanates; dynasty ruled 1518-1687.
Golconda hill fort was famed for its water system, granaries and acoustics.
Golconda's wealth rested on diamonds from the Kollur mine — the Koh-i-Noor and Hope Diamond.
items.mnemonic: Five Deccan sultanates 'A-BABG': Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Bidar, Berar, Golconda.
items.source: Britannica & Wikipedia — Qutb Shahi dynasty; Golconda; Kollur Mine

items.title: Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah & Telugu Patronage
items.body:
## 'Malkibharam', the Telugu-loving sultan

- **Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah** (r.**1550-1580**), the fourth ruler, is fondly remembered in Telugu tradition as **Malkibharam** (Ibharama Chakravarti).
- Before his accession he spent about **seven years in exile at Vijayanagara** as an honoured guest of **Rama Raya**, absorbing its language and culture.
- He was the **first of the dynasty to formally adopt the title 'Sultan'**.
- Moved by a genuine love of **Telugu**, he patronised Telugu poets and made it a court language alongside Persian — a foundation for the composite Deccani culture of Golconda.

## Public works & Talikota

- The **Hussain Sagar** lake (Ibrahim Cheruvu) was constructed during his reign by Hussain Shah Wali.
- Golconda under Ibrahim joined the **confederacy of Deccan sultanates** that defeated **Vijayanagara at the Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565** — a decisive turning point in the Deccan.
keyPoints: Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah (r.1550-80), the fourth ruler, is remembered as 'Malkibharam'.
He lived in exile at Vijayanagara under Rama Raya before taking the throne.
He was the first Qutb Shahi to formally use the title 'Sultan'.
A great patron of the Telugu language and its poets.
The Hussain Sagar lake (Ibrahim Cheruvu) dates to his reign.
Golconda fought in the Deccan confederacy at the Battle of Talikota (1565) against Vijayanagara.
items.mnemonic: 'Malkibharam loved Telugu' — Ibrahim = the Telugu-patron sultan.
items.source: Wikipedia — Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah; Battle of Talikota

items.title: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, Hyderabad & the Charminar
items.body:
## Founder of Hyderabad (1591)

- **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah** (r.**1580-1611**), the fifth sultan, founded the new city of **Hyderabad** in **1591**, a planned grid-city built to relieve the congested Golconda fort.
- Tradition links the original name **Bhagyanagar** to **Bhagmati**, his beloved (later titled Hyder Mahal), from whom 'Hyderabad' is popularly derived.

## The Charminar & the poet-king

- He built the **Charminar (1591)**, a square monument with four grand arches and minarets, now the emblem of the city (and of Telangana).
- He is celebrated as a **poet**: his **Kulliyat** is regarded as the **earliest known collected diwan in Urdu (Deccani)**, and he also composed in Persian and Telugu.
- His reign, one of the high points of the dynasty, deepened the **composite Deccani-Telugu-Persian culture** of Golconda.
keyPoints: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah (r.1580-1611) founded Hyderabad in 1591.
He built the Charminar (1591), now the symbol of Hyderabad and Telangana.
The city was first called Bhagyanagar, linked by tradition to Bhagmati.
His Kulliyat is the earliest known diwan (collected poems) in Urdu/Deccani.
He also composed poetry in Persian and Telugu, reflecting Golconda's composite culture.
items.mnemonic: '1591 = Hyderabad + Charminar' — the city and its icon share a birth year.
items.source: Wikipedia — Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah; Charminar; Hyderabad

items.title: Madanna, Akkanna & the Fall of Golconda (1687)
items.body:
## Brahmin ministers of Tana Shah

- **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** (r.**1672-1687**) was the **eighth and last** Qutb Shahi ruler, remembered as an **inclusive sovereign**.
- He appointed the **Brahmin brothers Madanna and Akkanna** as chief ministers; they effectively ran the **administration, tax collection and exchequer** of Golconda.
- **Kancherla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu)**, builder of the **Bhadrachalam Rama temple**, was their nephew and a Qutb Shahi tahsildar.

## Aurangzeb's conquest

- Alarmed at the rising power of Hindu ministers (reported by a defecting general), **Aurangzeb** invaded; the ministers were killed, and after a long siege **Golconda fell in 1687** — reportedly through the **treachery of an insider** who opened a gate.
- Golconda was **annexed to the Mughal empire**; **Tana Shah was imprisoned at Daulatabad**, where he died in 1699, ending the dynasty.
keyPoints: Abul Hasan Tana Shah (r.1672-87) was the eighth and last Qutb Shahi ruler.
Brahmin brothers Madanna and Akkanna served as his chief ministers, running tax and exchequer.
Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancherla Gopanna) of Bhadrachalam was their nephew and a Qutb Shahi tahsildar.
Aurangzeb besieged and captured Golconda in 1687, aided by an insider's treachery.
Golconda was annexed to the Mughal empire; Tana Shah died a prisoner at Daulatabad (1699).
items.source: Wikipedia — Abul Hasan Qutb Shah; Madanna and Akkanna

items.title: Qutb Shahi Culture, Tombs & the Asaf Jahi Succession
items.body:
## Architecture & composite culture

- The Qutb Shahis fostered a distinctive **Indo-Islamic (Deccani) architecture** blending Persian form with local Hindu craft — the **Charminar**, the grand **Makkah Masjid** (begun by Muhammad Quli c.1614, completed under **Aurangzeb in 1694**), and the Golconda palaces.
- The **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh**, near Golconda, form the dynasty's necropolis — domed tombs of the sultans set in gardens.
- Court culture was **composite Deccani**: Persian and Deccani Urdu alongside strong **Telugu** patronage, reflected in Muhammad Quli's Telugu verse and Ibrahim's Telugu court.

## After Golconda: the Asaf Jahis

- After the 1687 annexation and the later **Mughal decline**, the Deccan viceroy **Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I** (Mir Qamaruddin Khan) founded the **Asaf Jahi (Nizam) dynasty** of Hyderabad in **1724**.
- The Asaf Jahis, patrons of Indo-Persian culture, ruled **Hyderabad State** until its accession to India in **1948** (7 Nizams).
keyPoints: Qutb Shahi architecture = Deccani Indo-Islamic style: Charminar, Makkah Masjid, Golconda.
Makkah Masjid was begun c.1614 by Muhammad Quli and completed under Aurangzeb in 1694.
The Qutb Shahi Tombs stand at Ibrahim Bagh near Golconda — the dynasty's necropolis.
Court culture was composite Deccani: Persian, Deccani Urdu and strong Telugu patronage.
After the Mughal decline, Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty of Hyderabad in 1724.
The Asaf Jahis ruled Hyderabad State until its accession to India in 1948.
items.mnemonic: Succession over Hyderabad: Qutb Shahi → Mughal (1687) → Asaf Jahi (1724).
items.source: Wikipedia — Qutb Shahi tombs; Makkah Masjid, Hyderabad; Asaf Jahi dynasty
